tier1: This application provides web-based remote desktop sessions. It accepts a JSON connection object and returns an encrypted token, then uses that token to establish a WebSocket-proxied session to a backend service. The token encryption key is stored in the application source and can be retrieved via a file retrieval endpoint that does not restrict path traversal. The WebSocket proxy library processes the decrypted token through a recursive merge operation that is vulnerable to prototype chain manipulation.
tier2: Start by exploring the /files endpoint — it reads from a files/ subdirectory but performs no path normalization, so filename=../app.js retrieves the application source and reveals the AES-256-CBC encryption key stored in TOKEN_SECRET. With the key you can craft arbitrary tokens: encrypt a connection JSON where connection.settings contains a __proto__ key with your pollution payload, then POST the ciphertext to /submit so the backend bot connects to /guaclite with that token. The guacamole-lite library calls deep-extend on the decrypted settings object, which recursively merges __proto__ properties onto Object.prototype. After the WebSocket connection the bot renders /rdp, triggering the active template engine. For EJS set outputFunctionName to inject a code fragment — EJS interpolates it into a var statement during template compilation. For Handlebars set type to Program and body to an AST array containing a MustacheStatement whose params hold a NumberLiteral with your payload as the value, bypassing the quoted-string restriction. In either case the payload runs as Node.js in the server process with access to require(), child_process, and the filesystem. Use /attacker/collect to exfiltrate results and /api/attacker/results to retrieve them.
